title: Short Stuff: Women Pirates
summary: Short Stuff episode on women pirates. Josh and Chuck open by connecting the show Our Flag Means Death (female character passing as a man, queer romance) to real history of pirate ships as havens for women and gender-nonconforming people. They discuss the 1724 book "A General History of the Robberies and Murders of the most Notorious Pirates" attributed to the pen name Captain Charles Johnson (possibly Daniel Defoe, or publisher Nathaniel Mist), which mixes fact and embellishment, and how encyclopedias repeat its invented details. They then profile Anne Bonny, born in Ireland near Cork, raised in Carolina as a boy-disguised illegitimate child, who sailed with Calico Jack Rackham, and Mary Read, who also sailed with Rackham and fought fiercely. Their 1720 capture by pirate hunter Jonathan Barnett, trial in Spanish Town, Jamaica, and their pleading of pregnancy to avoid hanging are covered. The male crew was hanged. Mary Read reportedly died the following April, possibly in childbirth, and is buried in St. Catherine, Jamaica. Bonny's later fate is unknown, with speculation she returned to Charleston. The episode closes with sign-off and a short unrelated Packers stock joke. The hosts note the 'kissing' and 'both pulled off fake mustaches' stories are likely embellished.

segments.title: Opening banter and Our Flag Means Death
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the pirate theme and discuss the show Our Flag Means Death, including a female character passing as a man and a same-sex romance, and whether pirate ships were havens for queer women and gender-nonconforming people.

segments.title: A General History of the Pirates and its reliability
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the 1724 book A General History of the Robberies and Murders of the most Notorious Pirates was written under the pen name Captain Charles Johnson, possibly by Daniel Defoe or publisher Nathaniel Mist. Its mix of fact and embellishment makes it hard for historians to verify, and some encyclopedia entries repeat invented details. Mark Mancini of HowStuffWorks is praised for avoiding these.
topics: A General History of the Pirates

segments.title: Anne Bonny's early life and Carolina
segments.summary: Anne Bonny was born in Ireland near Cork, the illegitimate daughter of an attorney and his maid. Her father raised her dressed as a boy, and after the scandal cost him his practice, the family moved to Carolina, probably Charleston. The hosts note Carolina predates the split into North and South Carolina. Bonny later took the name Bonny, possibly from a pirate husband, and sailed with Calico Jack Rackham.

segments.title: Mary Read, piracy, capture, and trial
segments.summary: Mary Read, who also sailed with Rackham, was known for fighting, including beating a man who tried to assault her. Anecdotes about the two women meeting while disguised as men are likely embellished. Bonny and Read fought alongside Rackham's crew, were captured in late October 1720 after a brawl with mariners from Port Royal, tracked down by pirate hunter Jonathan Barnett, and tried in Spanish Town, Jamaica. Every male crewman was hanged.

segments.title: Pleading the belly and fate of the women
segments.summary: Bonny and Read both claimed pregnancy when sentenced, a practice called pleading the belly, which was confirmed by a doctor and spared them from hanging. Mary Read reportedly died the following April, possibly in childbirth, and is buried in St. Catherine, Jamaica. Anne Bonny was released, and her later life is unknown, with speculation that she returned to Charleston and had children.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the episode with a joke about booty and a Short Stuff sign-off, plus the show's production credit.
